business_problem: Dingdong Maicai needed more accurate demand forecasting, rider dispatch, and inventory optimization for time-sensitive fresh delivery, but its old big-data platform and algorithm environment were costly to run and hard to scale during peak periods.
solution_summary: Dingdong Maicai rebuilt its analytics and AI foundation on Huawei Cloud so forecasting and dispatch models could keep up with fresh-grocery delivery. The architecture separates storage and compute by using Object Storage Service OBS as a shared data layer for transaction, browsing, supply-chain, warehouse, weather, and fulfillment data, while MapReduce Service MRS provides elastic large-data clusters for offline and real-time analysis. On top of that base, the company transformed its algorithm platform with CCE Turbo, heterogeneous X86/Kunpeng/Ascend resources, and high-performance GPU compute instances so training jobs and temporary workloads can scale automatically during lunch and dinner peaks. Models then use user, order-time, rider, route, warehouse, product, and weather signals to recommend products, forecast front-warehouse demand, and generate optimal fulfillment paths.

solution_components.name: Object Storage Service OBS
solution_components.role: Stores the shared transaction, user, supply-chain, and fulfillment datasets used by analytics and AI workloads.

solution_components.name: MapReduce Service MRS
solution_components.role: Runs the elastic offline and real-time analytics jobs that feed forecasting and fulfillment models.

solution_components.name: Cloud Container Engine CCE
solution_components.role: Provides the container platform on which the cloud-native algorithm environment operates.

solution_components.name: CCE Turbo
solution_components.role: Supplies second-level elastic scaling and heterogeneous resource scheduling for model workloads.

solution_components.name: high-performance GPU compute instances
solution_components.role: Accelerate model training and AI inference for recommendation, prediction, and dispatch tasks.

solution_components.name: algorithm platform
solution_components.role: Hosts the recommendation, demand-forecasting, and dispatch models used in daily operations.

data_flow: Transaction, browsing, order, supply-chain, warehouse, rider, weather, and route data lands in OBS and is processed in MRS for offline and real-time analytics. The algorithm platform then trains and serves recommendation, demand, and dispatch models on CCE Turbo and GPU resources, returning predictions to warehouse stocking and delivery-routing workflows.
business_outcome: Dingdong improved prediction and dispatch quality while lifting large-data efficiency, lowering cost, and helping the business deliver faster service with higher order conversion and lower waste.
metrics: average monthly orders per user increased by more than 30%
storage cost reduced by more than 80%
architecture_clues: The design explicitly separates storage and compute with OBS and MRS.
CCE Turbo mixes X86, Kunpeng, and Ascend resources for the algorithm platform.
GPU resources are shared across multiple containers for temporary AI training tasks.
The platform supports both real-time dispatch inference and offline demand forecasting.
